Breakfast and After School Club
Breakfast Club (run by Foulds):
About Breakfast Club:
If you are interested in using The Early Birds club, or require further information, please email the school office; office@fouldsp.org
The Early Birds Club at Foulds offers breakfast (at 8:20am) and fun activities for our children. This daily club is enjoyed by the children allowing parents to get on with their journey to work.
What do the children do once they have eaten?
We have lots of games to play, Lego, Playmobil, drawing and painting as well as a quiet corner with cushions and books.
Do I have to come every day?
No. Whilst the Early Birds Club is open every school day, you can book the days that you need on Arbor but always in advance.
The fee is £6.00 per day and £5.30 for a second child.
You book and pay via your child's Arbor account. Please note, your wraparound section of your account needs to have money in it, in order to book a place.
The school accepts a range of childcare vouchers but these need to be on the system in advance. Please ask the office for more information about this.
Ms McClean, one of our experienced and enthusiastic mealtime supervisors and TAs, ably assisted by other Foulds staff. All of our staff know the Foulds children well.
Where do I drop my child off?
Please park outside of the school (not in the car park) to drop your child off. Walk them to the gate by the Dining Hall. Please do not let your child walk through the car park without adult supervision - it is a working car park and can therefore be potentially dangerous.
After School Club (run by LBL):
Click the link below to book:
https://www.littleladybirdslondon.com/lblfoulds
LBL are delighted to have opened a club at Foulds School. We are a multi-activity club with the following activities and resources available:
Arts and crafts resources
Sports and outdoor equipment
Small world play equipment
Construction toys (Lego, Knex, Playmobil, etc.)
Imaginative play equipment
​We foster an atmosphere of fun, warmth and play. Children are encouraged to engage with different age groups, try new activities and develop their social skills. We do not encourage the use of technology at the club, nor do we provide electronic resources. We are happy for children to complete their homework whilst at the club and will provide an area for that to happen but we would not expect LBL staff members to assist with homework in place of a parent.
​LBL operates a free play philosophy and abides by the Play Work Principles (2004). Full details can be found on our website but the most fundamental idea is this:
All children and young people need to play. The impulse to play is innate. Play is a biological, psychological and social necessity, and is fundamental to the healthy development and well-being of individuals and communities.
Simply complete and return a registration form and emergency contact form via email – these are available on our website or by emailing LBLFoulds@gmail.com.
We operate an online booking system. This is essential for our Safeguarding regulations so all bookings must be made online. You can book as many or as few sessions as you need and you can also make same day, last-minute bookings as we know plans can change! We aim to be as flexible as possible in the interest of parents and their childcare needs.
Payment can be taken online via PayPal, BACS, childcare vouchers or the government Tax-Free Childcare scheme. LBL are registered with all childcare voucher providers. If you wish to pay with vouchers, please check the website in the new year for info or drop us an email and we’ll explain the process.
How much does it cost?
We have two types of session:
Full Session 3:30-5:45pm:
£10 per session (sibling discount)
​One Hour Session (this can be used for an hour straight after school or an hour after another club)
(no sibling discount)
​Do you offer snacks?
We serve a selection of sandwiches (no pork or shellfish) and fresh fruit or veg every day with drinking water. We operate a healthy eating policy and are a nut-free zone. Children are welcome to bring their own snacks if they wish but we would ask parents to ensure they are healthy and comply with our nut policy.
Our team is headed up by one of our current LBL team leaders who brings with her our LBL philosophy and high standards. Current guidance for play work advises a ratio of 1:30. LBL operates a ratio of 1:15 as a minimum.
All staff undergo the following in line with Safer Recruitment in Education and Safeguarding guidance:
Safeguarding training (annual)
Paediatric and/or basic first aid training
Food safety and hygiene training
Regular staff training with policy and procedure updates
How do I contact you?
https://www.littleladybirdslondon.com/lblfoulds

Clubs and Sports Teams
We offer a wide variety of clubs for children to enjoy and explore their talents. Some of our clubs are run by our own staff on a voluntary (unpaid) basis and these are free, although there may be a small charge for resources. Where clubs are run by outside providers then there is often a charge - please contact the office for details.
EXTRA CURRICULAR CLUBS AT FOULDS SCHOOL

Sports Club Availability & Ethos:
We aim to run a range of high quality sporting clubs across as many age ranges as possible. Most of our sporting clubs take place after school and on some days they take place both indoors and outdoors. They are extremely popular with the children, many of them fill up quickly or have waiting lists – please check with the club organiser as to availability and when/how to apply.
As an inclusive school we encourage all children to try out a range of sports e.g. all the clubs below are open to both boys and girls. We encourage all children to recognise that through sport they can learn and live our school values.
For a full list of our current clubs, please see the newsletter.
Sports Inter-School and Intra-School Team Selection
Children may, at times, be selected to represent the school at a competitive fixture. Children are selected according to criteria such as ability, attitude and consistency of performance. Where possible, we also hold open trials in PE lessons or after school in order for all children to try out for teams and events.
We further aim to increase participation by having B and C teams for inter-school events and arranging popular events such as Inter-House Football, Netball and Gymnastics to include more children. We also take part in events that involve all children including intra-school events such as Sports Day and inclusive inter-school competitions like the Year 6 Marathon.
Whilst we endeavour to offer opportunities to as many children as possible, when it comes to competitive fixtures, team places are often limited, and the children understand that being in a club does not guarantee selection for the school team. Team selection can sometimes be bittersweet in that whilst some children are proud of being chosen, others are disappointed; in all areas of life we will encounter disappointments as well as successes and it is important that children learn resilience. We hope therefore children enjoy their clubs first and foremost - both the social aspect and developing their sporting ability. Selection for a team should be treated as a welcome bonus to this.
At Foulds we have strong links with local sports clubs to provide pathways from Foulds' PE lessons and Foulds' Clubs to enjoying and developing these sports outside of school.
Our experienced sports clubs organisers have a wealth of knowledge and would be happy to talk to you regarding the below as well as other avenues to pursue sports outside of school.

Safeguarding & E-Safety
It is extremely important that we keep our children safe and secure at all times. In order to do this we have a variety of systems and protocols in place which we ask parents to support and fully adhere to at all times.
A secure entry system with intercom
CCTV cameras are placed around the school site
On-site parking is restricted to school staff only
A member of the SLT stands at the entrances every morning
All staff are issued with photo identity lanyards
Adults authorised to visit the school site are required to sign in and out and wear visitors' lanyards at all times
All adults working regularly with children (more than three times in a month) will be subject to a DBS check
All staff, including supply teachers and other adults working with children, are given information about how to report concerns
Extra-curricular clubs must provide the school with qualification certification and DBS
All staff receive safeguarding training annually, with regular updates throughout the year.
Staff, governors, parents and children sign an Acceptable Use Agreement for safer internet use
Whilst all of our staff are responsible for safeguarding in Foulds, there are some key roles:
Kim Sanett is the Designated Safeguarding Lead
Amy Ingall, Luke Morley and Rebecca Tree are Deputy Designated Safeguarding Officers
Kavita Band is the designated Safeguarding Governor
Amy Ingall leads on whole school online safety

Our Governors
What Do Our Governors Do?
Governors are there to help the school run effectively. We are not involved in the day to day running of the school (termed operational matters) but are involved in helping the school to choose what direction it wants (termed strategic matters). Governors are involved in planning the strategic direction of the school, overseeing the financial performance of the school and ensuring that money is well spent and holding the head teacher and school leadership to account.
The Foulds Governing Body is made up of staff, parents, local authority members and community members. There are two committees, the Curriculum & Welfare Committee and the Resources Committee. Each committee meets once a term and the Full Governing Body (FGB) meets once a term also. The Resources Committee oversees, amongst other things, the school premises, the school budget, staffing and health and safety. The Curriculum & Welfare Committee oversees, amongst other things, pupil attainment and progress, children with special educational needs, safeguarding and pupil behaviour. Governors go into school at regular intervals to understand how the curriculum is delivered and talk to the children about their learning and provide feedback to their relevant committee. The chair of each committee then provides a report at the FGB meeting.
THE FOULDS GOVERNING BODY

Pupil Premium
Disadvantaged pupils make strong progress because of the quality and timeliness of interventions to help them with their learning. The sustained focus on their progress helps to diminish the difference between their outcomes and their peers, nationally.
What is Pupil Premium?
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011 and is additional funding that the government gives to schools for each pupil on roll where they are deemed to be disadvantaged.
Who receives Pupil Premium?
Pupil Premium is allocated to pupils in school year groups from Reception to Year 11 from low-income families who are registered for Free School Meals. It is also allocated for those who have been registered for Free School Meals at any point in the last six years, together with children that have been in care continuously for 6 months or more. Children that have been adopted from care are also eligible for this funding.
Who are our designated LAC Staff Members?
Miss Sanett and Mrs Kanji

School Day
Our school week is 33.33 hours.
The gates open at 8.35am each morning and close at 8.45am.
The register closes at 8.50am and children are marked as late after this time.
It is really important that your child comes in for the very start of the school day as the first session of each morning includes key skills learning which is essential for each child.
The school day finishes at 3:25pm. The gates open at 3:20pm but please note the gate will not be opened until all classes are back in the building eg if they have had PE last session.
There is a staff member always present at drop off and pick up times. If you have a question, please do come and ask or pop into the office. We ask that you talk to teachers at pick up time, not in the morning please.
NB If children are late to be dropped off or picked up on a number of occasions, parents will be called in for a meeting with the Deputy Head or Headteacher.

Sports Premium
What is PE and Sport Premium?
Since September 2013, the government has been providing additional funding for Physical Education (PE), to improve provision of PE and sport within primary schools.
This funding is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on provision of PE and sport in schools.
Funding for schools is calculated by reference to the number of primary-aged pupils (between the ages of 5 and 11), as recorded in the annual schools census.

How Foulds spent the 2024-25 sports premium funding?
CPD for all staff to have First Aid training
Continued membership of the Barnet Partnership for School Sport which allow entry to Borough's leagues, cups, competitions, festivals and access to CPD
Renewed subscription to Complete PE which maps and provides resources for all PE units for the 2 year cycle from EYFS to upper KS2
Swimming subsidies to ensure all children in KS2 attend swimming lessons, including those who need extra lessons to meet the government Year 6 targets
Invested in equipment to improve PE lesson, clubs, playtimes and outdoor classrooms
Set up a lunchtime club to support SEN children's engagement at playtimes
Provided cover to allow teachers and TAs to take teams to interschool PE competitions. This year saw us enter a record number of inter-school events including: Football (girls and mixed league, cup and events for Year 1/2, Year 3, Year 4, Year 5, Year 6 teams plus B, C teams and inclusive events), rugby, netball, Sportshall Athletics (indoor), Copthall track and field athletics, Cricket league and cricket tournaments, Cross Country, Dodgeball, Dance, Golf and Year 3/4&Year 5/6 Tennis
In addition to the above, funded by Sports Premium money, we also have teachers, TAs, parents and pupils all volunteering their time for free to create further sporting opportunities.
Thank you to all those who: volunteered to run extra-curricular clubs this year, were involved in inclusive events, ran interhouse competitions for Year 3/4 & Year 4/5 (Football, Netball, Gymnastics), KS1 & KS2 Sports Days and events outside the Sports Partnership such as the Year 6 Micromarathon with other local schools.
Thank you to the Sports Captains and House Captains and other Young Leaders for running daily lunchtime activities and supporting other sporting events throughout the year. Thank you to pupils involved in School Council and Pupil Voice for providing ideas and feedback.
Thank to Mr Dillon and MGM Cars for sponsoring two new football goals and to those who have supported at linked clubs in the community such as Old Elizabethans Cricket Club, Barnet Elizabethan RFC and Ravenscroft Park Tennis Club.
